questions: Compared with iteration 2 (16 mm footprint), does oval and s-bend progress rise above about 0.45 with the 12 mm footprint? If so, the footprint was blurring the centre signal.
Do line_loss_events stay near 1 to 1.3 on all three tracks with the 12 mm footprint, or do the outer sensors lose the tape more often?
Do max_error excursions still occur at the same bend locations, and do they start before or after a line-loss event?
What kp, ki and kd did you use? Does the signal stay monotonic across the 15 mm pitch, or is there a dead zone where the line sits between sensors?
If progress recovers but max_error stays at 0.063 to 0.065 m, would you accept a wheel_track of 0.10 in the next iteration without other changes?

intent: Test the footprint change alone. Keep the 60 mm span and y = 0.05 lead that recovered progress in iteration 2, and reduce sensor_size from 16 mm to 12 mm, as the iteration 2 feedback rule and Integrator request 1 specify. Expected: oval and s-bend progress rise above 0.45 (toward iteration 0's 0.66 on the oval), line_loss_events stay near 1 to 1.3, and max_error stays about 0.06 to 0.065 m. If progress does not recover, the footprint is not the cause and the next lever is wheel_track 0.10.
learning: Iteration 2 showed that restoring y = 0.05 recovers most progress (oval 0.273 to 0.405, s-bend 0.109 to 0.423) and keeps line losses near 1 with the 60 mm span, so the lead was the main cause of the iteration 1 collapse. Progress is still just below the 0.4 threshold on the oval, so this iteration tests the 12 mm footprint in isolation. max_error stays at 0.063 to 0.065 m on every track across three iterations, so it is not sensitive to span, footprint or lead. Turn rate through wheel_track is the next untested lever for it.
rationale:
Iteration 2 restored the y = 0.05 lead while keeping the 60 mm span and 16 mm footprint. It recovered most of the progress lost in iteration 1: oval progress rose from 0.273 to 0.405, s-bend from 0.109 to 0.423, and the score from 64.6 to 133.7. So the shorter lead (y = 0.03) was the main cause of the collapse. Line losses stayed near 1 (1.2, 1.1, 1.0), which the wide span keeps under control. max_error stayed at 0.062 to 0.065 m on every track, so off-track excursions are still transient and are not caused by tape loss.

The feedback rule I wrote last iteration says that if progress stays below about 0.4 with line losses near 1, the 16 mm footprint is probably blurring the centre signal, and the next step is a 12 mm footprint with the 60 mm span. Oval progress is 0.405 and s-bend is 0.423, right at that threshold. Iteration 0, with a 12 mm footprint, had the best oval progress (0.664), although its span was 40 mm. The footprint is the one sensing variable not yet isolated at the 60 mm span.

I therefore change only the footprint, from 0.016 to 0.012, and keep the 60 mm span (x = -0.03, -0.015, 0, 0.015, 0.03), y = 0.05, and all body, wheel and mass values. With a 15 mm pitch and 12 mm footprints, the 25 mm tape is always covered by at least one sensor across the array, and the outer sensors keep a graded signal. I expect progress to move back toward 0.5 or higher, line losses to stay near 1 to 1.3, and max_error to remain near 0.06 m. max_error is the untested lever for the next step, which is wheel_track 0.10 if progress recovers and max_error stays on its plateau.
